weak_links: USMCA impact (-$1.3B) is an estimate: ~335k Mexico-built US sales (Maverick, Bronco Sport, Mach-E; 2025 sales partly extrapolated) x ~$25k import value x 25% x ~50% non-US content, plus ~$0.25B for parts. The content share and Ford's ability to price it through drive the range.

A withdrawal notice is a six-month warning, not withdrawal itself; it may be a negotiating move later withdrawn. Kalshi's thinner KXUSMCAOUTCOMES-27 prices a US withdrawal notice in 2026 at about 13% (last trade, wide spread) versus 6% here.

Tariff-repeal impact (+$1.0B) uses Ford's own 2026 net tariff cost (CFO: 'better than $1B'); repeal would also help importing rivals, so Ford's relative advantage on US-built trucks shrinks: the net could be smaller.

House control decides only half of a tariff repeal: the Senate (Kalshi D ~64%) and a presidential veto also stand in the way; the book's 0.05 for a Democratic House already reflects that. Book row for House Democrats' 0.45 'make: alone' (floor disapproval votes) is not used: disapproval resolutions do not apply to Section 232 tariffs, which are what Ford pays.
California 2035 rule: the EPA waiver is already revoked, so relaxing it matters only if courts restore it; the +$100M is a rough per-vehicle compliance-cost estimate on ~130k California sales.
Michigan governor (Benson: 'subnational agreements with Canada', book p 0.45) checked and left out: a state agreement cannot change federal tariffs Ford pays, so no dollar effect.

entries.hook: Ford's Mexico-built Maverick, Bronco Sport and Mach-E enter the US with USMCA relief from the 25% Section 232 auto tariff.
entries.event_plain: the US gives notice to leave USMCA before 2027

market.question: Will Trump try to leave the USMCA before 2027?
market.rules_summary: Yes if the United States submits a notice of withdrawal from the USMCA before Jan 1, 2027. The 'before 2027' rung is used: it is the only rung with trades, and the cost would start once withdrawal takes effect six months after notice (2027).

impact.formula: Losing USMCA treatment puts the 25% Section 232 tariff on the full value of Mexico-built vehicles instead of only non-US content: ~335,000 US sales a year (Maverick ~160k, Bronco Sport ~125k, Mach-E ~52k) x ~$25,000 import value x 25% x ~50% non-US content now untaxed = ~$1.05B, plus ~$0.25B for USMCA auto parts losing their exclusion = ~-$1.3B a year before pricing actions. Low: 40% content, half passed on in price. High: 60% content plus engines/transmissions from Mexico and Canada at full 25%.
impact.timing: from mid-2027 if withdrawal takes effect six months after a notice
